title: Young's Modulus

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Mechanical Properties of Solids

explanation: Young's modulus is the ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain within a material's elastic limit, measuring its stiffness/resistance to stretching or compression along one dimension. A higher Y means the material is stiffer (small strain for a given stress) — steel has a much higher Y than rubber, which is why steel resists stretching far more for the same applied stress.

workedExample.scenario: A wire of length 2 m, area 1×10⁻⁶ m², stretches by 1 mm under a 100 N force.

commonMistakes: Forgetting ΔL must be in the same length units as L before dividing (a common unit-conversion slip, e.g. mixing mm and m).
Assuming a material that stretches easily (large ΔL for small F) has a HIGH Young's modulus — actually the opposite: easy stretching means a LOW Y.
genZNote: Steel's Young's modulus said 'I don't bend easily' — rubber's said the complete opposite.
